newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices flat, await the Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices flat, await the Fed.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds mainly were pegged around flat in early afternoon trade on Monday, as the market stalled ahead of Tuesday's Federal Reserve policy makers meeting, as they waited to if rates would be raised.

Traders said that while there was cash looking for investments, few players were willing to make bets this close to the crucial meeting. And with few new issues coming to market on Monday, activity was even more subdued than usual at the start of a week.

"They're not a lot of people willing to do anything, they did what they had to do position-wise on Thursday and Friday," a trader said. Later, he added: "I think there's a lot of money around...but they're not going to spend a lot of it today and tomorrow morning before the Fed announces whether or not they will tighten."
The Wall Street Community was sharply divided about the outcome of the Fed's Tuesday meeting, with a slight majority leaning towards unchanged, according to a Reuters poll.

In terms of new issues, the market was looking ahead to Nevada's competitive sale on Tuesday of about $285 million of general obligation bonds, as well as Wednesday's sale by New York City of nearly $740 million of general obligations.
Referring to the Nevada sale, the trader said: "That's kind of going to be the high-grade sale of the week."

The retail presale period for New York City ends at midday on Tuesday, and on Friday, the city had only obtained about $66 million of retail orders, falling short of the over $100 million of orders it placed on the first day in a previous sale.
City officials said they would take full advantage of the retail order period, and the bonds were expected to attract considerable retail interest, as is typical.
Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, a gauge of the secondary market, stood around $1.05 billion, straddling the border between abundant and lean supplies.
In the secondary market, Orange County, Florida, School Borad of 2017, which have a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.64 percent, unchanged.
And Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey revenues of 2026, which carry a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.68 percent, also flat.

June municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade rose three ticks to 116-16/32, while the June U.S. Treasury bonds fell two ticks to 109-29/32. This left the MOB spread at a strong plus 205 ticks. Traders said the lack of supply of new issues was a key feature driving up the spread.
